before.description: Logix and Digital Research agree to develop a new CP/M version for Logix Aurelia. DRI fully owns the resulting CP/M version and makes it available to other vendors through non-exclusive licensing. The collaboration adds a text-mode TUI, smart-device and card integration, XIP cartridge support and named user areas.

clauses.statement: DRI retains the right to implement the TUI libraries and FlexiBUS support in CP/M versions for non-Logix computers.

Logix supplies Aurelia platform requirements, interface knowledge and integration work; DRI develops and integrates the CP/M operating-system changes. They cooperate on interoperability and qualification for Aurelia. Hardware, devices and cards remain platform deliverables rather than DRI hardware-manufacturing obligations.

DRI fully owns the new CP/M version and its CP/M software enhancements developed through this collaboration. DRI may offer and license that version to any other vendor on non-exclusive terms. Aurelia compatibility and Logix collaboration confer no exclusive CP/M distribution right on Logix. Hardware and technology ownership are not transferred by this software-ownership term.

Provide a text-mode TUI: pseudo-window interfaces, menus and shared interaction conventions that make applications usable through a consistent text-screen interface. Integrate the Logix TUI standard with CP/M software services.
Support smart devices and expansion cards using Plug and Execute and FlexiBUS technologies, with documented CP/M integration so qualified devices and cards can expose their functions to applications.
Support XIP cartridges and their software interfaces so suitable programs can execute in place from cartridge ROM on compatible hardware.

Allow names to be assigned to CP/M file User Numbers, presenting user areas as named directory-like locations. This supplies a named organisation layer over User Numbers without asserting a new hierarchical filesystem.

before.description: BPI Systems accepts Adam’s $150,000 investment in exchange for a 33% fully diluted interest. clauses.statement: Adam agrees to subscribe $150,000 of new capital into BPI Systems for development and working capital. BPI accepts the subscription; it is company funding rather than a payment to existing owners.

after.title: Birmingham funerals, inheritance and disposal of family assets
after.description: Operating as Adam Pleskot, Vincent spends 2 January to 2 February 1972 in Birmingham arranging the parents’ funeral, settling inheritance formalities and disposing of the family estate. After expenses he holds approximately GBP 6,000 and his remaining belongings for departure.

participant.role: protagonist; Vincent operating as Adam Pleskot after the identity takeover

inputs.description: The parents’ deaths and Vincent’s assumption of Adam’s identity create the need and opportunity to settle family affairs.
The estate includes the Birmingham house and saleable possessions, together with an insurance claim for the single family car destroyed in the fatal accident.

steps.description: Handle the formalities connected with inheriting the parents’ wealth.

Sell the house and saleable possessions, settle the insurance claim for the destroyed family car and receive its payout, handle any salvage formalities, and settle estate and funeral expenses. Retain approximately GBP 6,000 net and the remaining belongings for departure.

outcomes.description: The parents’ funeral has been arranged and inheritance formalities handled.

Adam holds approximately GBP 6,000 in net estate proceeds, including the crashed car’s insurance payout, and his remaining belongings after disposal and expenses. The car is not sold as a usable vehicle. The insurance amount is unspecified and is included in, rather than added to, the GBP 6,000 total.

change.title: Revise Incorporation of Computer business
change.reason: Keep the earlier company-formation event inside the process by making it the start; move DRI founding into steps and include leadership recruitment.

before.title: Incorporation of Computer business
before.description: Adam establishes the computer-business organisation and its initial engineering and software partnerships across Logix Tech, AION Labs and AION Software, in cooperation with Digital Research, BPI and other participants. This formation phase begins with the DRI founding and funding milestone and ends with Tim Paterson’s recruitment.

participant.role: semiconductor research and development participant after its formation
software development participant after its formation

inputs.description: Adam’s established investment activity provides a financial basis for forming and supporting the computer businesses.
Adam contributes knowledge of future demand and technology while keeping its origin private.

steps.description: Establish Logix Tech, AION Labs and AION Software.
Establish the separate secret future-equipped facility supporting chip design.
Agree development and distribution cooperation with independent BPI Systems.

outcomes.description: Logix Tech, AION Labs and AION Software are established, with initial engineering infrastructure and supporting access to the separate future-equipped facility.
Cooperation with DRI and BPI is established under the existing agreements. DRI and BPI retain the independence and rights specified in those agreements.
Gordon Letwin and Tim Paterson have been recruited for the developing computer business.

after.title: Incorporation of Computer business
after.description: Adam establishes Logix Tech, AION Labs and AION Software and develops their initial leadership, engineering and software partnerships with DRI, BPI and others. This formation phase starts with the three companies on 23 November 1974 and ends with Tim Paterson’s recruitment.

participant.role: semiconductor research and development participant after its formation
software development participant after its formation

inputs.description: Adam’s established investment activity provides a financial basis for forming and supporting the computer businesses.
Adam contributes knowledge of future demand and technology while keeping its origin private.

steps.description: Establish and fund independent DRI as the operating-system cooperation partner.

Approach the prepared shortlist and recruit separate CEO, CFO and CTO roles for Logix Tech in San Jose, AION Labs in Cambridge, England, and AION Software in Copenhagen. Agree operating responsibilities and financial controls; individual appointees remain unspecified.
Establish the separate secret future-equipped facility supporting chip design.
Agree development and distribution cooperation with independent BPI Systems.

outcomes.description: Logix Tech, AION Labs and AION Software are established, with initial engineering infrastructure and supporting access to the separate future-equipped facility.
Cooperation with DRI and BPI is established under the existing agreements. DRI and BPI retain the independence and rights specified in those agreements.
Gordon Letwin and Tim Paterson have been recruited for the developing computer business.
